He played professional basketball with the [Derby Rams](/wiki/Derby_Rams "Derby Rams") in the [British Basketball League](/wiki/British_Basketball_League "British Basketball League").

Calvin Coolidge headstone in Plymouth Notch, Vermont

Coolidge died suddenly of [coronary thrombosis](/wiki/Coronary_thrombosis "Coronary thrombosis") at The Beeches on January 5, 1933, at 12:45 p.m., aged 60.[[193]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGreenberg2006154–155-198) Shortly before his death, he told an old friend, "I feel I no longer fit in with these times."[[194]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESobel1998a410-199) Coolidge's funeral was held at Edwards Congregational Church in Northampton, Massachusetts. Many prominent politicians attended the service, including Coolidge's successor Herbert Hoover, Vice President [Charles Curtis](/wiki/Charles_Curtis "Charles Curtis"), Chief Justice [Charles Evans Hughes](/wiki/Charles_Evans_Hughes "Charles Evans Hughes"), and Secretary of State [Henry L. Stimson](/wiki/Henry_L._Stimson "Henry L. Stimson"). All the New England governors were also present.[[195]](#cite_note-200)

President Herbert Hoover ordered flags at half-staff for 30 days and military and naval honors on the day of the funeral. Hoover sent out a special Message to Congress to inform them of the former president's passing.[[196]](#cite_note-201)[[197]](#cite_note-202)

Coolidge was then taken back to Vermont, where he was buried in [Plymouth Notch Cemetery](/wiki/Plymouth_Notch_Cemetery "Plymouth Notch Cemetery") in [Plymouth Notch, Vermont](/wiki/Plymouth_Notch,_Vermont "Plymouth Notch, Vermont"). The nearby family home is maintained as one of the original buildings on the [Calvin Coolidge Homestead District](/wiki/Calvin_Coolidge_Homestead_District "Calvin Coolidge Homestead District") site. The President Coolidge Historic Site was started in 1947 by the state of Vermont when they purchased and rehabilitated the childhood home of his mother. This was the first of multiple restoration projects in Plymouth Notch. In 1956 Coolidge's son [John](/wiki/John_Coolidge "John Coolidge") donated his father's boyhood home to the state of Vermont.[[198]](#cite_note-203)

Orbit of Mars and other Inner Solar System planets

Mars's average distance from the Sun is roughly 230 million km (143 million mi), and its orbital period is 687 (Earth) days. The solar day (or [sol](/wiki/Mars_sol "Mars sol")) on Mars is only slightly longer than an Earth day: 24 hours, 39 minutes, and 35.244 seconds.[[199]](#cite_note-201) A Martian year is equal to 1.8809 Earth years, or 1 year, 320 days, and 18.2 hours.[[2]](#cite_note-NasaFactSheet-3) The [gravitational potential](/wiki/Gravitational_potential "Gravitational potential") difference and thus the [delta-v needed](/wiki/Delta-v_budget "Delta-v budget") to transfer between Mars and Earth is the second lowest for Earth.[[200]](#cite_note-Petropoulos_Longuski_Bonfiglio_2000_pp._776–783-202)[[201]](#cite_note-Taylor_2020-203)

The axial tilt of Mars is 25.19° relative to its [orbital plane](/wiki/Orbital_plane "Orbital plane"), which is similar to the [axial tilt of Earth](/wiki/Ecliptic#Obliquity_of_the_ecliptic "Ecliptic").[[2]](#cite_note-NasaFactSheet-3) As a result, Mars has seasons like Earth, though on Mars they are nearly twice as long because its orbital period is that much longer. In the present day, the orientation of the [north pole](/wiki/North_pole "North pole") of Mars is close to the star [Deneb](/wiki/Deneb "Deneb").[[21]](#cite_note-barlow08-23)

Mars has a relatively pronounced [orbital eccentricity](/wiki/Orbital_eccentricity "Orbital eccentricity") of about 0.09; of the seven other planets in the Solar System, only [Mercury](/wiki/Mercury_(planet) "Mercury (planet)") has a larger orbital eccentricity.
